key_insight: In severe chloride-rich atmospheric exposure, painted reinforced concrete can be a practical alternative to galvanized steel, with the carbon-steel-in-concrete system showing unexpectedly strong anticorrosive performance.
engineering_relevance: For infrastructure exposed to aggressive marine or industrial atmospheres, the study suggests prioritizing reinforced concrete with high-performance coatings over galvanized steel when long-term corrosion resistance is critical.
method: Built concrete specimens with carbon steel or galvanized steel reinforcement and three commercial coating systems (CS1, CS2, CS3).
Characterized concrete, coatings, and steels using physical, barrier, mechanical, and chemical tests.
Used salt spray exposure plus electrochemical monitoring (OCP, EIS, polarization resistance) to assess corrosion behavior.
evidence_signal: Across long-term salt spray and electrochemical evaluation, the traditional carbon-steel-and-concrete system performed best, and the coating-specific differences were hard to separate because overall anticorrosive performance was strong.
watch_item: The abstract suggests the coating effect may be difficult to distinguish under the tested conditions, so field validation and longer exposure studies are still needed before broad implementation.
paper_title: Painted Reinforced Concrete as an Alternative to Galvanized Steel in Chloride-Rich Environments
